source: Quiz 3 - Sessions 1-4: Model Size, Thinking, and Skills
question: According to the lecture, which kind of skill is reasonable to write or edit directly in chat, without a coding-capable agent?

options.text: Any skill whose instructions fit on less than one printed page
options.feedback: Length was not the deciding factor. A short skill can still depend on code, and a long one may be nothing but prose instructions.

options.text: Any skill that has already been used successfully at least once
options.feedback: A track record does not change what a skill needs for editing. A code-bearing skill still wants a coding-capable agent no matter how well it has run so far.

options.text: A skill you expect to run only a handful of times before discarding it
options.feedback: How often you plan to use a skill does not decide where to write it. A throwaway skill can still need real code, and a heavily reused one can be pure instructions.

options.text: A skill that is pure writing or formatting instructions with no code behind it
options.feedback: With no code to run or test, the whole skill is prose, so it can be drafted and revised conversationally -- the way the class talked through rewording the narrative-versus-expository line.
